title: Avalanche sign Cale Makar to 8-year, $163.2 million extension — largest contract in NHL history
content:
The Colorado Avalanche have signed star defenseman Cale Makar to an eight-year, $163.2 million contract extension, his agency announced on Friday.

The deal is the largest in NHL history, as is the $20.4 million average annual value.

The 27-year-old Makar, drafted No. 4 in 2017, is already one of the most decorated players in franchise history. Since debuting in the Stanley Cup playoffs and scoring in his first game, he has won the Calder Trophy as the NHL’s rookie of the year, the Norris Trophy twice as the league’s top defenseman, a Stanley Cup championship and the Conn Smythe Trophy for playoff MVP. He has been a Norris finalist each of the past six seasons. Internationally, he was on Canada’s 4 Nations Face-Off-winning team in 2025 and won silver at the 2026 Olympics.

Makar registered 20 goals and 79 points in 75 games last season, helping the Avalanche to the Presidents’ Trophy with the NHL’s best record. He dealt with an injury in the playoffs that kept him out of the first two games of the Western Conference final, which Colorado lost in four games to the Vegas Golden Knights. In 2024-25, he won the Norris and became the league’s first defenseman to score 30 goals in a season since Mike Green in 2008-09.

Makar’s most impressive season arguably came in 2021-22. He won the Norris with 28 goals and 86 points in 77 games, then had 29 points in 20 playoff games as Colorado captured the Stanley Cup.

“We’re lucky because we’re watching greatness,” then-teammate Erik Johnson said during that postseason run.

Makar is entering the final season of a six-year deal that is worth $9 million annually, after which his extension will kick in.

Makar’s contract is a massive raise from his current deal. The Avalanche clearly wanted to have him under contract long-term. With the rising cap, that presumably was going to happen only if the deal came with a huge AAV.

Makar will be 36 when his new contract ends, so general manager Joe Sakic guarantees he will have him through his prime. The percentage of the cap Makar’s AAV will occupy will decrease over time as the cap ceiling continues to rise.

This is also the last summer teams are allowed to give eight-year contracts, with a seven-year limit taking effect under a new collective bargaining agreement.

Makar will be the first NHL player to make more than $20 million in a season. The salary cap for the 2027-28 season, when Makar’s new deal goes into effect, is expected to rise to $113.5 million. The maximum cap hit a player can have is 20 percent of the upper limit, which would make the individual player max $22.7 million next summer. But because that’s only a projection, the maximum a player can sign for now is 20 percent of the current $104 million cap, $20.8 million.

Makar tops Kirill Kaprizov ($136 million deal signed last summer) as the most lucrative contract in NHL history. His new deal will presumably also have an impact on the negotiations between star defenseman Quinn Hughes and the Minnesota Wild. — Peter Baugh
